paragraphs.text: The plumbing scope should be filed as a subsequent (S) filing under the existing GC job number, rather than as a new unrelated job number, if it is part of the same construction project and property. DOB guidance says all filings for the same construction project should use the same job number with an extension; a subsequent filing adds new scope of work and work types, and it may use a new/different applicant. It is separately processed and may be permitted before the initial GC filing.

For submission, the initial GC filing must first be submitted—not remain in pre-filing status. The FAQ says a subsequent filing can then be initiated and submitted until an LOC has been issued for the initial filing. The guide directs users to select “Subsequent Filing” from the Filing Action column beside I1. The materials acknowledge that a subsequent can be created before I1 is submitted, but its populated fields will not update until I1 is submitted; they do not fully resolve any broader rule on creation timing before I1 submission.

Completion handling depends on the initial job type. The general guidance says an LOC is requested separately for each initial and subsequent filing. But for NB or Alteration-CO filings, the specialized FAQ says not to request an LOC for the subsequent filing: its status remains Permit Entire, while only I1 changes to CO issued. The initial job type was not supplied, so this completion branch cannot be selected here.

supportingSourceUses.claim: [PDF page 5](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf#page=5) — Page 5 of 38 JOB FILING /APPLICATION A job is an application submitted for a construction project on a property, which can vary from making alterations to a single unit in an existing building or to constructing a new building with many units. A job filing/application is submitted to obtain a Work Permit to perform a specific type of construction. All filings related to the same construction project should have the same job number and then an alphabetic and numeric extension that indicates the filing type and sequence: I - Initial, S - Subsequent, and P - Post Approval Amendment (PAA). • Initial Filings (I1) – The first or initial job filing created for a construction project. • Subsequent (S) - A subsequent filing is an additional filing under the same job filing number that allows an applicant (the same one on the initial or a new applicant) to add new scope of work and new work types to a job on the same property. A subsequent filing can have a different review type (standard plan examination/professional certification) than the initial filing. Once submitt ed, a subsequent filing functions as a separate appli cation. It can be permitted before the initial is permitted and a Letter of Completion (LOC) is requested separately on each filing. • Post Approval Amendment s (PAA) - A Post Approval Amendment or PAA is for making changes to a filing after it has been approved. To create a job fi ling, log into DOB NOW: Build and from the dashboard select +Job Filing. Then select the Job Type, Work Type (s), and Filing Review Typ e. Subsequent applications are strongly encouraged. All filings with the same job number will go to the same plan examiner or team and the Records Management Fees are paid on the initial filin g only. It is also beneficial to have one job number to connect all of the work on a project.

[PDF page 6](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf#page=6) — Page 6 of 38 To create a subsequent filing, select Search from the dashboard. Select BIN Search to find filings on the BIN or select Job Number Search if the job number is alr eady known. From the Filing Action column next to the initial (I1) filing, select action Subsequent Filing. J ob T ypes Alteration – Questions about the scope of work are provided to determine if the filing is an Alteration CO or an Alteration CO – New Building with Existing Elements to Remain. If No is the answer for all the questions, then the filing is an Alteration (does not require an amended CO). • Alteration required to meet New Building requirements? (Yes = Alteration CO – New Building with Existing Elements to Remain) • Alteration is inconsistent with the current Certificate of Occupancy? (Yes = Alteration CO) • Alteration in occupancy or use? (Yes = Alteration CO) • Alteration is a major chan ge to exits? (Yes = Alteration CO) • Alteration in number of stories? (Yes = Alteration CO if Building Type is 3 Family or Other) Full Demolition - The dismantling, razing, or removal of all of a building or structure, including all related incidental opera tions. The Full Demolition Types are: New Work, Emergency Declaration, Immediate Emergency Declaration, Emergency Work Order, and Precept. A registered design professional (PE/RA) is required as the applicant on a full demolition filing when one or more of the f ollowing conditions are met: • Building is greater than 3 stories in height • Building is greater than 5,000 square feet per floor • Building is not detached • Demolition Is using mechanical equipment • Foundation is not being removed

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — When can I submit a subsequent job filing? — Subsequent filings can be initiated and submitted after the initial job filing is submitted (not in pre-filing status). Users no longer have to wait until the initial filing is approved. A subsequent filing can be submitted anytime until an LOC has been issued for the initial filing.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — Do I have to request a Letter of Completion (LOC) for a subsequent job filing? — Yes, an LOC needs to be requested for each filing, initial and subsequent filings.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — If an initial job application is filed as professional certification can the subsequent application be filed as a standard plan filing type? — Yes, initial and subsequent jobs can have different filing types.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — Can a subsequent filing have a different design applicant than the initial filing? — Yes, the applicant on an initial filing and a subsequent filing can be different. If the applicant is the same, one application can be submitted if the work types are eligible to be combine filed.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — Do I have to pay the record management fee on a subsequent filing? — No, the $165 record management fee is now charged only once on the initial filing and is no longer a fee on subsequent filings.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — Can I have an open PAA for the initial filing and a subsequent filing at the same time? — Yes.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — How can I make a minor change to a legalization filing? — Post-Approval Amendments (PAA) are not allowed on filings that include legalization work. If a change needs to be made, a subsequent filing will be required or the job must be withdrawn and refiled. For Boiler Equipment filings the only option is to withdraw and refile the job. In addition, permits cannot be renewed if the job includes legalization work.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — I have a subsequent filing in pre-filing status and some of the fields are grayed out? How do I complete these fields? — Fields from the subsequent filing are populated from the initial filing (I1). The fields will not update on the subsequent filing until the I1 is submitted. To prevent this issue, we recommend completing as much of the I1 as possible before creating the subsequent filing.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > New Building and Alteration-CO — Do I need to request a Letter of Completion for the subsequent filing of an NB or Alteration-CO filing? — No, the status of the subsequent filings will remain Permit Entire. Only the status of the initial (I1) filing will change to CO issued. If a Temporary CO is issued, the status of the initial job will remain Permit Entire until the Final CO is issued.

attributedClaims.text:
DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — When can I submit a subsequent job filing? — Subsequent filings can be initiated and submitted after the initial job filing is submitted (not in pre-filing status). Users no longer have to wait until the initial filing is approved. A subsequent filing can be submitted anytime until an LOC has been issued for the initial filing.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — Do I have to request a Letter of Completion (LOC) for a subsequent job filing? — Yes, an LOC needs to be requested for each filing, initial and subsequent filings.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — If an initial job application is filed as professional certification can the subsequent application be filed as a standard plan filing type? — Yes, initial and subsequent jobs can have different filing types.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — Can a subsequent filing have a different design applicant than the initial filing? — Yes, the applicant on an initial filing and a subsequent filing can be different. If the applicant is the same, one application can be submitted if the work types are eligible to be combine filed.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — Do I have to pay the record management fee on a subsequent filing? — No, the $165 record management fee is now charged only once on the initial filing and is no longer a fee on subsequent filings.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — Can I have an open PAA for the initial filing and a subsequent filing at the same time? — Yes.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — How can I make a minor change to a legalization filing? — Post-Approval Amendments (PAA) are not allowed on filings that include legalization work. If a change needs to be made, a subsequent filing will be required or the job must be withdrawn and refiled. For Boiler Equipment filings the only option is to withdraw and refile the job. In addition, permits cannot be renewed if the job includes legalization work.

DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > Subsequent Filings — I have a subsequent filing in pre-filing status and some of the fields are grayed out? How do I complete these fields? — Fields from the subsequent filing are populated from the initial filing (I1). The fields will not update on the subsequent filing until the I1 is submitted. To prevent this issue, we recommend completing as much of the I1 as possible before creating the subsequent filing.

attributedClaims.text: DOB NOW: Build Frequently Asked Questions > New Building and Alteration-CO — Do I need to request a Letter of Completion for the subsequent filing of an NB or Alteration-CO filing? — No, the status of the subsequent filings will remain Permit Entire. paragraphs.text: Because the initial filing is approved, the appropriate action is a Post Approval Amendment (PAA) in DOB NOW: Build to revise the approved scope and drawings. The Applicant of Record who filed the original filing must file it; only one PAA may be in progress. A PAA is unavailable if the filing includes legalization, but the supplied fact says it was not submitted for legalization. Revised PDF plan sets and a DPL1 must be uploaded, and the change description must be entered in the Plans/Work (PW1) Comments field. The Department reviews the PAA, and approval is not established until that review results in approval.

The filing must disclose the revised scope and plan changes in PW1 Comments. If approved plans are being changed, upload a complete plan set: new unapproved sheets without an approved stamp and previously approved DOB-stamped sheets; after PAA approval, that uploaded plan set replaces the prior set. The PAA fee is a flat $100 when filed, and an estimated job-cost increase or decrease triggers fee recalculation; any increase difference must be paid. Filing Review Type, application/location address, Applicant of Record information, owner information, and building type are not editable. The supplied guidance gives incompatible directions about the specific Work on Floors field: the process page lists it as noneditable, while the FAQ says it can be changed with a PAA when adding or removing a floor, with PW3 updated for the changed estimated work cost. That field’s editability remains unresolved in these passages.

evidenceLimitations: The supplied passages conflict on whether the Work on Floors field is editable in a PAA; they do not resolve which instruction governs for this filing.
